title: DC-area forecast: Muggy with some showers today, then nicer days return
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Showers and maybe a rumble are with us this morning, especially I-95 and east, then tapering in coverage late morning into afternoon. Muggy highs only reach the mid-70s to near 80.

What’s next? Showers and some thunder may develop again this evening or overnight. Maybe a leftover shower early Sunday morning with decreasing humidity. Mostly sunny and pleasant Monday and Tuesday.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: A muggy Saturday with showers early, but maybe some dry time during the afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Saturday): Muggy with some showers and maybe a few rumbles passing through this morning. Because we’re toward the edge of a storm veering to our east, it’s uncertain if scattered showers continue during the afternoon, or if the afternoon ends up mostly dry – some sort of lull is favored. Areas south and east of the Beltway have the highest chance of more numerous, heavier showers overall. Highs only in the mid-70s to near 80 under mostly cloudy skies. Confidence: Low-Medium

Tonight: Scattered showers and a few thunderstorms are possible at times during the evening and overnight. Skies remain mostly cloudy, with lows ranging from the mid-60s to near 70. Some patchy fog is possible. Rainfall totals could range from 0.25 inches or less north and west of the Beltway to as much as 1 inch or more for Southern Maryland. The area in between is the most uncertain. Confidence: Low-Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Sunday): A few leftover showers could be around early Sunday morning before quickly ending. Skies gradually clear from mostly cloudy to mostly sunny. We should start to see some relief from the humidity as highs reach the low to mid-80s and dew points fall into the low to mid-60s (maybe even upper 50s by afternoon). Winds coming from the northeast turn a bit breezy, with late-day gusts of 15 to 20 mph. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: A quiet and comfortable one as skies remain mostly clear. Overnight lows range from near 60 to the mid-60s while humidity falls off further. Confidence: Medium

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Monday and Tuesday look to offer a dry and pleasant start to the workweek as high pressure builds into the region, bringing a welcome break from the humidity. Highs around 80 to 85 with mostly sunny skies and comfortable dew points in the mid- to upper 50s. Winds from the northeast remain light, around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

More typical August warmth and humidity returns Wednesday as a dip in the jet stream over the Great Lakes tracks east. With a breeze more from the south, highs climb into the mid- to upper 80s with increasing humidity (dew points rising into the low to mid-60s). A shower or storm chance could return by afternoon or evening. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 22

The powerful 1933 Chesapeake-Potomac hurricane slammed into Hampton Roads with near-100 mph winds and an 8-foot storm surge, devastating coastal Virginia before tracking north toward the DC region.
